title: Case 1: Administrative Tribunals (CAT & The L. Chandra Kumar Basic Structure Rule) (Article 323A • Writ Petition)
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 323A (Administrative Tribunals (CAT & The L. Chandra Kumar Basic Structure Rule)) of Part XIV-A (Tribunals). Relying on the core guarantee that Empowers Parliament exclusively to provide by law for the adjudication of public service disputes by administrative tribunals (leading to the Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 establishing CAT); interpreted by the historic 7-Judge Bench in L. Chandra Kumar... and citing L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable under Article 323A?
2. Does the Union Ministry / Central Authority's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 323A (Administrative Tribunals (CAT & The L. Chandra Kumar Basic Structure Rule))?
3. How does L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 323A (Part XIV-A).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 323A): Empowers Parliament exclusively to provide by law for the adjudication of public service disputes by administrative tribunals (leading to the Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 establishing CAT); interpreted by the historic 7-Judge Bench in L. Chandra Kumar...
